analysis: Changes are test-only. GLM5NextManagedLoadTests.swift: the synthetic fixture tokenizer gains <think>/</think> tokens (lines 120-121), and a new env-gated test, verifiedDigestExistsOnlyAfterEveryManifestFileVerified (lines 707-745), checks that load.verifiedArtifactSHA256 is nil before load and equals the manifest aggregate and WeightHasher output after load. It also checks that a same-size corrupted shard leaves the digest nil and the budget reservation released. This strengthens verification of weight integrity (T-012, T-027). The test is gated by DARKBLOOM_TEST_GLM5_MANAGED_SYNTHETIC=1, uses a synthetic self-generated artifact, and redirects the cache directory to a fixture-local path via ModelScanner.configureCacheDirectory with a defer restore. No production path, real weights, key material or network access is touched. No production code, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage behavior (T-041) is modified. The new file, GLM5NextOpenRouterCapabilityTests.swift (added, 487 lines), was supplied as metadata only, with no source text or head_text unit, so I could not inspect its content. The patch excerpt shows it is a test harness: a scripted CBv2 engine and a Jinja template tokenizer, with no weights or GPU. Because its body was unavailable, I cannot confirm it makes no external calls or leaves no residual state. There are no apparent security regressions in the visible changes. A pass over production code that consumes verifiedArtifactSHA256 (the weight-hash publication path) would be needed to assess the real attestation and routing impact; that code is not in this batch.
